hints: Focus on the reaction type first. Heating an alcohol with concentrated acid means dehydration by elimination of water.
Draw out butan-2-ol as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and see where the H can be removed from alongside the C-OH carbon.
Remember that but-2-ene can exist in two different spatial forms around the $\text{C=C}$ bond, while but-1-ene cannot, so count all distinct alkenes carefully.
walkthrough:
**Recognise dehydration**

Heating butan-2-ol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to form an alkene. The -OH leaves from C2 and an H is removed from a neighbouring carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_8 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the two positional isomers**

Remove H from C1 and you get but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$. Remove H from C3 and you get but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$. Both pathways are possible.

**Add cis-trans isomerism**

But-1-ene has $\text{CH}_2$ at one end, so no E/Z isomerism. But but-2-ene has two different groups on each $\text{C=C}$ carbon, so it exists as cis (Z) and trans (E) forms.

$$\text{total alkenes = 1 (but-1-ene) + 2 (cis and trans but-2-ene) = 3}$$

**Match to the options**

Only the set containing but-1-ene plus both cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene is complete. That is the set with three unbranched $\text{C}_4$ alkene structures.

options.A: Shows but-1-ene and only trans-but-2-ene. It is missing the cis-but-2-ene isomer, so it is incomplete. Students often forget that but-2-ene shows E/Z isomerism and count it only once.
options.B: Shows all three correct products: cis-but-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3$ groups on same side), trans-but-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3$ groups on opposite sides), and but-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$). This covers both elimination positions and both stereoisomers of but-2-ene.
options.C: Shows but-1-ene and only cis-but-2-ene. It is missing trans-but-2-ene, so it is incomplete. This is the opposite half of the same trap as in A.
options.D: Includes a branched alkene, 2-methylpropene $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2$, which cannot form here. The carbon skeleton does not rearrange from a straight chain to a branched chain in this dehydration. It also misses trans-but-2-ene.
